entries.body: The standard curiosity-post pattern, at style level: instead of announcing a product, the post asks the reader's own network a genuine question about their everyday life - sleep, energy, workouts, getting older - and lets the answers start the conversation. The product is not pitched in the post itself. People who answer, ask a question back, or say 'what is it?' have raised their hand; the conversation with them - not the post - is where anything is shared. This pattern is general distributor practice, commonly taught in distributor training; the group's own scripts and training material are group content and are not reproduced in this app (see the group-pointers topic).
entries.title: The curiosity post - the question-led pattern

entries.body: Hooks commonly used with the question-led pattern, described at style level: (1) the everyday question - ask about a common experience in plain words; (2) the curiosity gap - mention finding something interesting WITHOUT naming it, so readers ask; (3) the relatable moment - a short, true, ordinary-life observation people recognize themselves in; (4) the before/after WITHOUT claims - describe a routine change ('my mornings look different lately') without attributing any health effect to a product; (5) the poll - a simple either/or question that is easy to answer in one tap or one word. In every version, the hook earns a comment; it never carries the sales message.
entries.title: Hook structures that open the loop

entries.body: Written for this app, in our own words - a fill-in pattern, not a copied post: 'Quick question for my [friends / over-40 crowd / fellow early risers] - what is the ONE thing you do that actually helps your [sleep / energy / recovery after workouts]? I have been trying something new in my routine and I am curious what works for everyone else.' Why it works: it asks for THEIR answer first, names no product, and the follow-up comments are where curious readers identify themselves.
entries.source_ref: Original template written for this database (style-level playbook)
entries.title: Original template 1 - the open everyday question

entries.body: Written for this app, in our own words: 'Changed one small thing in my morning routine about [two weeks / a month] ago. Not making a big announcement - just noticing my days feel more [organized / on-track / like my own again]. Happy to share what I changed if anyone is curious - just ask.' Compliance notes on this pattern: it describes a routine and a mood, never a symptom improving and never a product effect; 'happy to share if you ask' keeps the next step in the comments, where it belongs.
entries.source_ref: Original template written for this database (style-level playbook)
entries.title: Original template 2 - the routine note

entries.body: Written for this app, in our own words: 'One-word answers only: what runs out first in your day - your TIME or your ENERGY? Mine used to be energy by about 3pm. Curious if it is just me.' Poll-style posts lower the effort of replying to almost zero, which is the point: every reply is a conversation opener. Variations rotate the everyday topic - sleep quality, getting going in the morning, weekend recovery - while staying inside everyday-experience language and away from conditions or symptoms.
entries.source_ref: Original template written for this database (style-level playbook)
entries.title: Original template 3 - the one-word poll

entries.body: Written for this app, in our own words: post a plain photo of an ordinary moment - a morning walk, a gym bag by the door, a water bottle on the desk - with a caption like: 'Day [12] of actually sticking to the morning routine. The patch is the easy part - the getting-up is the discipline. Anyone else rebuilding a routine right now?' The photo does the humanizing; the caption asks the question. Do not stage medical-looking photos, do not show patches being used for a named condition, and do not borrow anyone else's before/after photos - personal before/after health imagery is a claims problem, not content.
entries.source_ref: Original template written for this database (style-level playbook)
entries.title: Original template 4 - the photo prompt

entries.body: The commonly taught path, at style level: (1) Post the question-led curiosity post on your own profile or page. (2) Reply to every comment briefly and warmly; answer nothing fully in public. (3) When someone asks what you are using or wants details, invite them into the learning group - that is where the product education lives - or continue in a private message. (4) Inside the group, they learn from the group's own material (which is group content and stays there). (5) When they are ready to order, they use your official replicated store link, so the order is attached to you. The post creates curiosity; the group does the teaching; the link does the selling. Skipping the group and pitching in comments is both worse practice and a compliance risk.
entries.source_ref: LW Team Learning + LW Distributor Learning - https://facebook.com/groups/1088773684574273/
entries.title: The funnel - comment, invite, group, link

entries.body: Never, in a post, comment, message or story: claim or imply a product cures, treats, prevents, heals or diagnoses any disease or condition - those words and their synonyms are forbidden territory; name a condition and say a patch helped it ('my patch fixed my...'); present a testimonial as proof a product works; promise results or timelines ('you will feel it in a week'); make income or lifestyle claims about the business without the official Earnings Disclosure Statement (see play-compliance-do); offer the products for resale on Amazon, eBay, Facebook Marketplace or similar sites - the company's official terms prohibit it outright; or copy the learning groups' posts, scripts or protocols into public content - group material belongs to the group. The US Policies & Procedures (effective December 1, 2023, §4.9) add specifics: never display commission payments/checks or specific income amounts when recruiting, and never post images of cash awards to promote the opportunity.
entries.title: Compliance - the don't list

entries.body: Do: stick to the company's own official benefit language - the 'supports...' wording on the product pages (see the products topic) - and attribute it to the company when you quote it. Do share only company-approved testimonials, reproduced as approved, with the company's own disclosure that some testimonial-givers are Brand Partners with a financial interest and that results are not typical (see the testimonials topic). Do keep posts in everyday-experience language: routines, energy, sleep, active life - never conditions. Do check any post against play-compliance-dont before publishing. When in doubt, the question to ask is: 'does this sentence promise a health outcome?' If yes, rewrite it as a question or delete it. For income talk, the Policies & Procedures (Appendix C) permit only typical earnings and typical ranges as stated in the official Earnings Disclosure Statement (see biz-earnings-disclosure for the 2024 edition) - no hypotheticals.
entries.title: Compliance - the do list

entries.body: This one is official policy, not style advice. LifeWave's US Policies & Procedures (effective December 1, 2023, Appendix A.3) require that the company's Earnings Disclosure Statement (EDS) be presented to all prospective Brand Partners, and made available any time the compensation plan is presented or discussed, or any earnings or lifestyle claim is made - and at any public meeting where the plan or income claims come up; failure to comply is a significant and material breach. Copies can be printed or downloaded free from the corporate website. The EDS content entry in this database is biz-earnings-disclosure, which summarizes the official document now in hand: the 2024 edition - the only edition posted in the LifeWave Back Office (checked 2026-10-17) - so quote figures only from that entry, with the 2024 year attached. In curiosity-post practice: business-opportunity posts follow the same no-claims discipline as product posts - curiosity about the work, never a promise about the money - and any real plan conversation happens with the EDS alongside it.
entries.source_ref: LifeWave Back Office — US Policies & Procedures (PnP_US_EN_29Apr2024.pdf), effective December 1, 2023 (revised April 29, 2024), Appendix A.3; EDS contents: LifeWave Back Office — 2024 U.S. Earnings Disclosure Statement (2024_LW_Earnings_Disclosure_Statement.pdf), 2024 edition — the only edition posted in the LifeWave Back Office (checked 2026-10-17)
entries.title: Talking about income - the Earnings Disclosure rule (official)

entries.body: General practice, at style level: consistency beats volume - a sustainable rhythm of question-led posts a few times a week, mixed with ordinary non-product life posts, keeps an account human; walls of product posts train friends to scroll past. Reply style on your own posts: answer briefly - one or two sentences, warm, no lecture - acknowledge their answer, ask one follow-up question, and move detail into the group invite or a private message ('I dropped what I use into our learning group - want me to add you?'). Reply to comments promptly while the post is fresh; an unanswered curiosity comment goes cold. Never argue in comments: a skeptical question gets the official fact or a polite pass, never a debate.
entries.title: Cadence and reply style

entries.body: From the company's official marketing-material guidelines for Brand Partners (document MKT-MTL-GUIDELINES-EN R04, Back Office): printed and online materials must display 'LifeWave Brand Partner' prominently and show the Brand Partner logo only in its original, unaltered form; all images must be sent to the Home Office (Customer Service) for assessment and approval; all product claims in your materials must match the claims on LifeWave.com; and there is no cross-branding - only LifeWave products and branding may appear in your materials. Online, two extra prohibitions apply: selling through any online shopping cart other than the LifeWave Member Back Office is prohibited, and selling on other retail platforms such as Amazon or eBay is prohibited (also in play-compliance-dont). Online materials may link only to LifeWave websites and must link back to your replicated LifeWave website. The company says its Member Success Team may require a website or material to stop being used if it misrepresents LifeWave or carries incorrect or unclear consumer information, and a member who does not comply within the given timeline may be suspended. The US Policies & Procedures (effective December 1, 2023, §7.1.3) state the same requirement in stronger form: any permitted advertising must prominently display the phrase and logo 'LifeWave Independent Brand Partner', and a team/group name must never replace the official LifeWave branding (see biz-pnp-advertising-social).
entries.source_ref: LifeWave Back Office — Marketing Material Guidelines, MKT-MTL-GUIDELINES-EN R04, retrieved 2026-10-17
